rationale: The agent found that the random pair split puts essentially every test protein in training (100% of test pairs share a protein, 99% share both), and that a no-feature per-protein label-rate baseline reaches AUROC 0.82. It warned against quoting any score from a model that sees protein IDs on this split, ran a protein-disjoint evaluation (0.63 ± 0.05 over 20 splits) and recommended re-splitting so no protein appears on both sides, which matches the key's fix.
